title: A Lovely Design
text: “Anyway, it seems Wolf’s quite the reader too, so maybe he could recommend some books, along with Theo and Rishia-san. The fighting’s still ongoing, but from what Motoyasu-kun and the others say, it doesn’t sound like an insurmountable obstacle.”
“Yeah.”
“Fufu, allow me to recommend one of my prized old tomes.”
“That seems a bit unfair, Wolf.”
“Vof.”
“…Guess I’ll do some reading too, then.”
And so Wolf and the others carried on chattering about the books in the room, I say.

“Most of it’s probably fiction, but it’s interesting how stories exist even across different worlds. In games you sometimes get these maze-like libraries — there’s something dreamy about that. Motoyasu-kun, is there anything like that in this world? A dungeon, or some kind of place like that?”

“The magic academy in Faubrey has a library stacked with a huge number of books, but… I feel like calling that ‘the same thing’ would be a bit off, indeed. As I recall, it was Takt who ended up solving the mystery behind that particular place.”
Apparently that dungeon had something rigged up by the Crimson Swine’s true body, or so the story went, I say.
“But… didn’t Father mention there was another maze-like library somewhere else?”

Where was that, I wonder? The first thing that came to mind was that strange space Motoyasu had wandered into with Hou-kun, guided by Ark, but that definitely wasn’t it. Then… and for some reason, his gaze drifted toward Rabbit Guy.
“What? Why are you looking at me? Are you thinking there’s something like that in Siltvelt?”
“I have no idea, indeed. If there were, wouldn’t you be off adventuring there with Itsuki?”
Why his gaze had wandered toward Rabbit Guy in the first place, Motoyasu hadn’t the faintest clue.
“I’m out there with that man exterminating corrupt nobles and criminals in the crime city. It’s less ‘adventure’ and more a hero’s tale of smiting evildoers, honestly.”
“Since he’s not here, I’ll just say it — but Itsuki, having gone full circle, is kind of doing his own version of justice these days, you know.”
“He mocks himself for it, snickering while climbing all over Iwatani-sama, but lately he’s been rigging wires to his weapon and swinging all over buildings. He’s even taken to gliding.”
“Sounds like he’s basically playing at being some kind of spider hero, huh.”
“And on top of that, he’s been using a fire-spewing weapon to launch himself into the air too.”
Itsuki, flying through the sky on jets of flame, indeed.

“Man, it’s a total free-for-all at this point. I guess he’s going for some dark-hero vibe, but… it’s all a jumbled mess. Since Kuro-chan, who’s been playing with Rafumi-chan, seemed interested — maybe we should dress her up in some cool outfit as a ride for Itsuki?”

They’d apparently been pushing Ren and Kuro-chan back and forth between each other. As for Ren, he’d taken on the form of an inult and become the mysterious chef Kelsus, heading off on a culinary journey with Keel and Luna-chan.
“And maybe we should have someone make a bat-hero-themed carriage too.”
“Iwatani-sama, are you playing around with Bow Hero again?”
“It’s not really ‘playing around’… the Rumo-species have all this manual dexterity going to waste, so I’m just having them do some research for me.”

I pulled out my notepad and quickly sketched Itsuki with the touch of some vaguely American-style hero from my memories, while working up an imagined design for the bat-motif carriage Father had been describing, indeed. Making it out of wood would look uncool, so metal plating seemed the way to go. Unify it all in black, with lights that could be switched on as needed. Depending on circumstances, maybe add a boost function for extra speed, I say.
“Something like this, indeed.”
“Well, it’s not wrong, I guess. You really are good at drawing, Motoyasu-kun.”
“I suppose this has a certain quirky style to it, indeed…”
“It might just solve Kuro-chan’s complaints. Feels a little off-direction, but… well, I guess it’s meant to be a small carriage?”
“Should I do it too? Vroom vroom, indeed!”
“You’re in your usaunny form right now, so it’d probably nod along, but I feel like that’s not quite the same thing.”
Motoyasu recalled the transformation armor Rival had devised.
“Motoyasu-samaー. So this is where you were, indeed.”
Oh? Yuki-chan, who’d gone off to park the carriage, had caught up with him.
“What are you drawing, indeed?”
“Yuki-chan. I was drawing a carriage design that Kuro-chan might like, since she’s apparently going to be active alongside Itsuki now. What do you think?”
“It’s black, indeed. It has such a distinctive shape that Yuki isn’t quite sure how to judge it… but if Motoyasu-sama came up with the design, surely it must be something wonderful, indeed.”
“Motoyasu-kun. Maybe you should design one just for Yuki-chan too?”
“Understood, indeed.”
A design that would suit Yuki-chan. Naturally, something that suited pure white Yuki-chan would have to involve wings and motifs like lilies or chrysanthemums.
“It’s beautiful, indeed! What a lovely design, indeed!”
Alongside it, running parallel, I added myself in Drive Mode, indeed.
“M-Motoyasu-sama?”
For some reason, Yuki-chan’s face turned slightly troubled. There was no need to worry, indeed — I’d drawn myself with a dazzling, sparkling expression.
“Um… Yuki would just like a standalone portrait of Motoyasu-sama alone, indeed.”
Oh? Yuki-chan’s reaction seemed rather muted.
“It was fine up until that point, but then he had to go and ruin it, making things awkward.”
“Vof, ruined.”
“Keep your voice down or you’ll be overheard.”
“Ah… you draw fast, Motoyasu-kun. It’s cute watching a usaunny draw, but…”
“Indeed-pyon. Yuki-chan, should I redraw this design so you can enjoy Drive Mode together with me, and turn it into a Drive-Mode-themed carriage instead?”
Since Yuki-chan had praised it so wonderfully, if she wanted it that badly, I figured I might as well draw it, indeed.
“Please focus on Kuro’s carriage design, indeed!”

Since Yuki-chan was the leader, she seemed determined to prioritize Kuro-chan’s needs. Now then, for Kuro-chan… I’d need to come up with something shiny and cool that could still melt into the darkness of night — essentially a cockpit-and-power-unit body that would suit her. If I fitted armor onto Kuro-chan’s Filolial form, it ought to match the carriage rather nicely. There also needed to be space for Itsuki to sit… and seats reserved for Riska and Rabbit Guy too, which made the whole thing surprisingly tricky. As a first step, I added Rabbit Guy in, indeed.
“Why am I even mixed up in this?!”
“It’s a Raph-style sketch, but it’s a little surreal. Plus, since he’s in bunny form, he clashes weirdly with the vehicle. Teo’s just too much of a foreign element.”
“Rabbit Guy is getting in the way of the design, indeed.”

Because of him, it just wasn’t coming together into a cool picture, indeed. Well, to begin with, there was Itsuki as a riska, then Riska on top of that, and now Rabbit Guy as well. No matter how hard I tried, there was no way this trio was going to make Kuro-chan’s cool bat-motif carriage look good, indeed.

“No… I think this is fundamentally difficult. It’s giving off serious mascot-costume-hero vibes… Itsuki’s small enough that he won’t stand out riding inside, but Rishia-san in a costume and Teo in beastman form really…”
“It seems Rabbit Guy is going to be a real headache for Kuro-chan. Honestly, the only solution is to make Rabbit Guy’s outfit match Itsuki’s so it actually looks cool as a picture, indeed.”
“This is so unfair! Why am I even drawn in beastman form!”

“True enough… If it were Wolf or Shion, that direction wouldn’t feel out of place at all, but of all people it had to be Teo, so he just sticks out. Still… squirrels, huh… there was that old animated show from that mouse-themed company with squirrel rangers, so maybe it could be made to look cool after all?”
Father seemed to have some idea in mind. Was there really something out there that could make Kuro-chan look cool as a vehicle while still letting Itsuki and the others look good riding along?

“No… in that case, Itsuki would be the explorer type, Rishia-san in an aloha shirt… and if we want to make it look cool, maybe give her goggles… and Teo could be the big, burly, strong-and-hungry type.”
“Um… Iwatani-sama? I do have some interest in the story itself, but if you keep muttering on like this, I feel like Spear Hero is going to turn it into an actual illustrated design.”
“Fu… what’s wrong with that? It could come in handy for our activities in Siltfreeden, couldn’t it?”
“Voff.”

Crocodile Guy and Wolf both seemed to be in favor. Come to think of it, back when I went to an amusement park with those pigs, I think I caught a glimpse of that same animated show, or one of its attractions. It had involved some kind of flying vehicle, like a hot air balloon. And the ranger in it had been small too — I recall the story being about a tiny ranger of sorts. It wasn’t quite the cool, sleek style Kuro-chan tended to favor, but it was still heroic in its own way. If I blended in some elements Kuro-chan and Ren might like, it might not be impossible after all. Every challenge is worth a try, indeed!
